theme: 3 terms on writing and calling functions

terms.definition: A named block of code that does one job and can be run again whenever you call it by name.
terms.example: I moved the date formatting into a function so both screens can reuse it.

terms.definition: A named input that a function declares so the caller can pass a value in.
terms.example: The method takes one parameter, the user ID, so pass it the ID of the signed-in user.

terms.definition: A word written before a value in a function call that tells the reader what that value is for.

video.description:
Learn to talk about functions in Swift: Function, Parameter and Argument Label, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Function - A named block of code that does one job and can be run again whenever you call it by name.
Parameter - A named input that a function declares so the caller can pass a value in.
Argument Label - A word written before a value in a function call that tells the reader what that value is for.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Function - A named block of code that does one job and can be run again whenever you call it by name.

dialogue.title: Pull request: the same code in two places
dialogue.setting: Morning stand-up and pull request review

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Morning, Jake. In your pull request, I see the same date code in two screens.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. I copied it from the home screen. It was quick.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Quick today, painful tomorrow. Let's put it in a function.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Okay. So I write one function, and both screens call it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. A function has a name, does one job, and you can run it again anytime.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What does it need from the caller? Only the date.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then add one parameter. The parameter is the input the function declares.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the parameter is called date, and the caller passes a real value.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Careful with words. The name inside the function is the parameter. The value you pass is the argument.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, I mixed them up in my comment. I will fix it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No problem. Now look at the call: format(d, true). What does true mean?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hmm. I forgot. It is for the short style.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That is why we use an argument label. Write format(date: d, short: true).

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I see. An argument label makes the call read like a sentence.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And you can hide an argument label with an underscore, when it adds nothing.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. For the first parameter I will hide the argument label, and keep it for short.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Perfect. Then delete the two old copies.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Already done. One function, one parameter, and a clear argument label.
I moved the date code into one function for both screens.
